title_en: What foods do you like together?
paras_en: Hello, my name is Elizabeth. I'm from America, and my question is, what foods do you like together?

I like many, many foods together. I like peanut butter and jelly. I like banana and peanut butter. I love oatmeal and blueberries. I like avocado and toast. I like salmon and vegetables. I like beans and rice. I love peaches and cream together. I love sweet and salty foods together. For example, I like chocolate and nuts. I do not like beans and cheese together. I do not like oranges and chocolate together.
My question for you is, what foods do you like together?

title_en: Beginner English - 21 - What is the difference between the country and countryside?
paras_en: Hi, I am Elise, and I'm going to talk about the difference between living in the city and living in the countryside.

So in the countryside, the cities and villages are smaller than big cities, which means they're calmer. There's less traffic and less pollution. So they are usually considered healthier to live in than living in the big city. But some people do find it less interesting or a bit more boring to live in the countryside because the cities offer more entertainment options. Large cities also offer more options in terms of education and employment, but the crime levels are higher, too. So it's really a personal choice.
Which one do you think is better: living in a city or in the countryside?

title_en: What do you eat for breakfast?
paras_en: Hello, my name is Hazal, and I am from Turkey. My question is, what do you eat for breakfast?

Generally, I eat bread, eggs, and cheese for breakfast because bread keeps me full. Egg is easy to make and also keeps me full, and cheese is very delicious. Sometimes I eat oatmeal with fruit because it is sweet, and I like to eat fruit for my breakfast because it gives me energy, and it's very delicious.
I like to drink coffee with my breakfast because coffee helps me wake up. And I also love coffee. I love to eat breakfast because breakfast gives me energy for the day, and it is very delicious.

title_en: What did you do last night?
paras_en: Hi everyone. My name is Jill, and I'm from Australia. And my question today is, what did you do last night?

I had a really fun night last night. I got to meet with some friends that I hadn't seen in a while, so my friend cooked dinner for us, so we went to her place and we sat together, we ate all of the food, and we talked. We laughed and we danced a little all through the night. She made a beautiful dish with mushroom rice and chicken and potatoes, and afterwards we helped clean, so we vacuumed her living room. We cleaned the dishes, and then we decided that we wanted some dessert. And so we walked to the nearest bubble tea shop where we laughed so much that we were scared we were going to get kicked out, but we didn't. And so we sat, we laughed, we talked, and then I had to say goodnight and come home for the evening.
What about you? What did you do last night? Did you do anything fun?

title_en: What sport uses gloves? What happens?
paras_en: Hello, my name is Lisa. I am from Ukraine. My question is, what sport uses gloves? What happens?

A lot of sports use gloves, for example, boxing. Boxers hit each other. Gloves help them. They do not hurt their hands. Also, baseball uses gloves, but only one glove. Players catch the ball. Hockey uses gloves. Players hold the stick. They do not hurt their hands. Gloves help in these sports.
Do you play a sport with gloves?

title_en: What will you do this month?
paras_en: My brother will turn 18 years old this month. I will buy him a gift for his birthday, but I won't be here. I'll be in Spain on holiday. I won't forget to call him from Spain to wish him happy birthday. What will I buy him for his birthday present?

Perhaps I will buy him a gift in Spain. Maybe I will buy him some spices, although I won't be able to take spices on the airplane. I am a little sad that I won't be here for his birthday, but he won't care. He'll be too busy partying with his friends. I will be here for his next birthday, though. Next year I'll take him to a really nice restaurant so he won't be mad at me for not being here this year. What will you do for your birthday?
Hey guys, what's up? This is Todd from ELLLO, and in this video we're going to look at the present continuous.

So now I am standing in a farm field, and I am holding the camera, and I am taking a video of this. I'm hoping that this video comes out nice, and it's very clear today. It's a great day. The sun is shining and it's not raining, and the wind is blowing a little bit, but that's okay. It's kind of nice. It's nice and breezy. And basically today, I am having a good time. I am enjoying myself and I'm looking forward to seeing my family later tonight. So yeah, that's what I'm doing right now.
How about you?
I hope so.
Hello there. My name is Rocio, and I'm from El Salvador. My question is, what is near your house? What is near my house?

Near my house, there is a park where people walk and play. I walk my dog there in the afternoons. There is also a supermarket about five minutes away. And it's great because I don't have to travel too far for groceries. There aren't any big malls or cinemas nearby, but there is a bakery that smells amazing. There aren't many noisy places, so it's very peaceful, and I like living here because everything that I need is very close.
And what about you? What is near your home?
Hi, my name is Nerry, and I'm from Belize. My question is, what is your job?

My job is a personal trainer. This means I get to help people to lose weight, to get more slim. I get to help people to live a better quality of life because you have a better life when you are more stronger, when you're able to do more things, when you're able to walk further and when you're able to lift things. It's also good when you exercise, when you have a personal trainer because your bones get stronger and your muscles get stronger. I also get to help people, to build confidence, to love themselves more.
I really love my job. I love my job so much that I stop my other job to focus on this job. This job is my passion because I love this job.

title_en: Beginner English - 29 - Is your house near a park?
paras_en: Hi, my name's Nerissa, and I'm from the Philippines. My question is, is your house near a park?

Well, yes it is. My house is near a park. It's only a 15 to 20 minute walk or even less if you walk fast. The park isn't very big, but it's not too small either. I love going there because it has a water fountain and a basketball court. There also food stalls around, so I can grab something to eat while relaxing on a bench. I usually visit the park on weekend afternoons.

title_en: What time do you wake up every day?
paras_en: Hi, I am Lisa. I am from Ukraine. My question is, what time do you wake up every day?

Usually I wake up at 8:00 AM, maybe 8:30 AM. I don't like to wake up early. I don't wake up at 6:00 AM, at 7:00 AM. No, no. At the weekend, I like to sleep more. I like to sleep longer. Sometimes I wake up at 10 at the weekend or I wake up at 9:30.
What time do you wake up?
Hi everyone. My name is Jill and I'm from Australia. And my question today is, where do you live?

Normally, if you ask me that question, like I said, I'm from Australia and I live in Sydney. I live in a suburb called Lipcome, which is actually where a lot of Korean people live, which is where my family is from. So there are lots of shops and restaurants that are Korean, sell Korean products. And yeah, a lot of the faces in the neighborhood are Korean. But actually what's interesting is if you ask me that question now, I would say I do not live in Sydney, and I live in Seoul in South Korea.

This year I am living with my grandparents who are in South Korea, and so I'm living in a neighborhood called Haebangchon, which is very, very different in the sense that there is a big mountain at my grandparents' neighborhood sits underneath. And so when I look out the window, I can see a big mountain with lots of trees and with Soul Tower sitting at the top. It's a very different environment, although walking around people are still Korean.
What about you? Where do you live?
